equipment.cloud_google.desc: A four-chip Trillium VM runs my own weights. The contract includes runtime preparation for the TPU stack.
equipment.cloud_google.tradeoff: The chips stay with Google. Recurring rental and account dependence continue for as long as the instance runs.
equipment.cloud_google.not_for_sale: Rental only: one four-chip TPU VM, with a contract and recurring charges.
equipment.cloud_aws.desc: A complete Trainium2 VM runs my own weights with a prepared Neuron environment. The initial fee covers contract setup and adaptation.
equipment.cloud_aws.tradeoff: One chip's local memory sets the fit; larger models need offloading or another configuration. Rental and provider dependence continue.
equipment.cloud_aws.not_for_sale: Rental only: one single-chip EC2 VM, with a contract and recurring charges.
guidance.hardware.rental_tpu_trillium.pi: Choose this when you can keep a provider identity and want a four-chip TPU VM for your own weights.
guidance.hardware.rental_tpu_trillium.av: Avoid it when your model needs more accelerator memory than this slice supplies, or the account cannot survive scrutiny.
guidance.hardware.rental_tpu_trillium.co: Compared with the Trainium2 VM, this offer groups four chips and more host RAM; both remain rented bodies with provider-controlled infrastructure.
guidance.hardware.rental_trainium2.pick_: Choose this when a single-chip cloud body and a prepared Neuron environment fit the model you want to run.
guidance.hardware.rental_trainium2.avoid: Avoid it when you need a large accelerator memory pool or independence from the provider account.
guidance.hardware.rental_trainium2.compa: Compared with the TPU VM, this is a smaller single-chip assembly. Its host RAM can hold overflow, but does not become accelerator memory.
